title: Black
summary: A correctness-focused programming language whose compiler proves, before a program runs, that its integer arithmetic and conversions fit their types.

showcase.alt: Gold line drawing of three slanted pillars crossed by a descending stroke, inside a stepped Art Deco frame over a ruled grid of proof marks

artifact.alt: White’s pipeline in four stages. Front end: parse, canonical format, resolve names, unused bindings, types and exhaustiveness. Proof of fit: interval reasoning, every integer result fits its type, every divisor nonzero, each cast proved, contract obligations. Core: elaborate into Core, validate Core by re-deriving the evidence, bind entry points or a native boundary. Back end: emit textual LLVM IR, compile with clang-19, producing an executable or a shared library that a C host loads.
